chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The Prophet Dawood (peace be upon him) passed away suddenly on Saturday, so the birds shaded him with their wings;
and Musa, the Speaker with God (peace be upon him), passed away in the wilderness, so a shrieker cried out from the sky: 'Musa (peace be upon him) has died — and which soul will not die?'

key_terms.التِّيه: The Tih, the desert/wilderness in which the Children of Israel wandered for forty years; the place of Musa's death
key_terms.صَائِحٌ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ: A shrieker from the sky — a heavenly announcer of the death of Musa
key_terms.كَلِيمُ اللَّهِ: Kalim Allah — 'the one spoken to by God directly', a special title for Prophet Musa (AS)
key_terms.مَفْجُوءاً: Suddenly, unexpectedly — denoting that Dawood's death came without warning

ai.seo_question: How did Prophet Dawood and Prophet Musa die according to hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates from the Prophet (SAWW) accounts of how two major prophets, Dawood and Musa (peace be upon them), died. Dawood died unexpectedly on Saturday and was honored by birds shading his body, while Musa died in the Tih desert and his death was announced by a heavenly voice with the universal reminder that every soul must die. This hadith is part of the chapter on causes of death and is intended to remind believers of the inevitability of death, using the examples of great prophets to emphasize this truth.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abdul Rahman Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The Prophet Dawood<sup>as</sup> passed away suddenly on the day of Saturday, so the birds shaded him<sup>as</sup> by their wings;

and Musa<sup>as</sup>, the Speaker with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, passed away in the wilderness, so a shrieker shrieked from the sky: ‘Musa<sup>saww</sup> has passed away, and which one would not be dying?’
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Prophet David died suddenly on a Saturday and birds provided shadow over his body.
Moses died in the wilderness where he had lost his way. A voice cried from the sky, “Moses has died! Who is he that does not die?””’
